response:
No tools were used; everything below is hand derivation, so treat it as leads to replay, not as checked results.

## Verdict

- **Two-holder overlap block:** strict product domination holds for every pair, for all arities (ternary and wide mixed), every overlap of at least two names, and either side having a single private name. The proof is below.
- **False pair through an outside name:** none, provided no pair of distinct names has |C| = 1.
- **Reading the parts without ages or flags:** yes on the exact table inside the class, with two unproved exclusions (exact zeros and forced pairs inside ternary collections with cycles). No at 128 draws.
- **Uniqueness against arbitrary full-law presentations:** not provable from a pair table; it can only be a collision check over the catalog.

## Exact two-holder table

Holders A and B are not-all-equal knots sharing s ≥ 2 names, with a ≥ 1 private names in A and b ≥ 1 in B. Inclusion-exclusion over "A all equal" and "B all equal" gives the count of allowed words:

N = 2^(a+b+s) − 2^(a+1) − 2^(b+1) + 2

Write α = 2^(a+1) − 2, β = 2^(b+1) − 2, σ = α + β + 2. Then N = 2^(s−2)(α+2)(β+2) − σ, and under the uniform weighting on allowed words:

| Pair | N·C |
|---|---|
| Two private names of A, or private of A with a shared name | −β |
| Two private names of B, or private of B with a shared name | −α |
| Two shared names | −σ |
| Private of A with private of B | +2 |

Note that A's private names carry the size of B, not of A.

**Domination.** For every pair x,y and every third name z in the block, N·|S_xy| > |S_xz|·|S_zy|. Every case reduces to one of:
- N > σ, which holds because N − σ ≥ αβ > 0 when s ≥ 2;
- 2N > αβ, which holds because N ≥ αβ + α + β + 2;
- N > β or N > α, which follow from N > σ.

**Sanity checks.**
- At s = 1 the private-private pair through the shared name gives 2N = αβ exactly, which is the multiplication rule at a single shared distinction.
- At a = b = 1, s = 2, direct counting gives N = 10 and C = +2/10 for the two private names, matching the table.

**Values for your cases** (the last column is the smallest entry, private of A with private of B):

| Case | N | Private pair in A | Private pair in B | Private–shared | Shared pair | A-private with B-private |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Two four-place, sharing three | 26 | none (a = 1) | none (b = 1) | −2/26 | −6/26 | +2/26 |
| Two four-place, sharing two | 50 | −6/50 | −6/50 | −6/50 | −14/50 | +2/50 |
| Four/five, sharing two | 106 | −14/106 | −6/106 | −14/106 (A), −6/106 (B) | −22/106 | +2/106 |
| Four/five, sharing three | 54 | none (a = 1) | −2/54 | −6/54 (A), −2/54 (B) | −10/54 | +2/54 |

## The outside name

- A shared name of the block is already held twice, so other parts attach only at private names.
- Complement symmetry of each attached part keeps the block's marginal uniform on its own allowed words, so the table above survives embedding.
- For c attached at z, C_ac·C_cb = C_az·C_zb·C_zc². With |C_zc| < 1 this is strictly smaller in size than C_az·C_zb, which is strictly smaller than C_ab. So there is no equality.
- If z = a, the product is C_ab·C_ac², again unequal unless |C_ac| = 1.

## General lead for more holders

For any set of not-all-equal holders:

N·C_xy = Σ over subsets T of holders that join x to y through shared names, of (−1)^|T| · 2^(joined pieces of T + names outside T)

N is the same sum over all T without the joining condition. This is exact and directly checkable.

- **Three holders in a row, both overlaps ≥ 2:** the smallest case (arities 3, 4, 3) gives N = 34 and the end-to-end pair through a shared name gives 20 against 68, so domination holds there. The leading term keeps a factor 2^(s−1) of margin in general. I did not close the general proof, because the lower-order terms need the same case split.
- **Closed rounds of holders:** the two ways around enter with signs set by their holder counts, so they partly cancel. The small cases I tried (three and four ternary holders meeting pairwise) stay nonzero (1/13 and 10/N). I have no theorem and no zero witness.

## Identifiability pitfalls

1. **Exact zeros.** A zero makes the multiplication test pass vacuously. The block and any tree of blocks have none. Ternary collections with cycles are unproved, so scan the catalog for C = 0 between names of one connected piece.
2. **Forced pairs.** A pair with |C| = 1 makes every third name complete a rate-sum-2 triple and breaks the outside-name argument. Scan for it.
3. **Implied triples.** Rate sum 2 means "never all equal", not "is a holder". Recover holders as an essential generating set.
4. **Disconnected cohorts.** Names in different pieces have C = 0. Split pieces first, never read that as a shared distinction, and do not let a connectedness filter drop legal unions.
5. **Arbitrary presentations.** A pair table is second-order only; different allowed-word sets can share it. Claim uniqueness only as "no collision in the catalog through 10, modulo one permutation", using a complete canonical form on exact rationals; sorted values are not complete.
6. **Ages.** The block law is the same whichever holder came first, so cross-age order is unidentifiable from the table wherever both orders are legal. Report it as that, not as a failure.
7. **The count alone.** Given the number of names, N fixes {a, b} and s within the two-holder class, by the binary digits of 2^(a+1) + 2^(b+1). Collisions with three-holder laws are open, so keep the count and the named table as separate results.

## Growth pitfalls

- **Parents from two old holders.** A child fed from loose names of two old holders that already overlap makes three holders meeting pairwise. That is outside part type (iii); label it, do not force-fit.
- **Lost essentiality.** A child lying inside one parent's names (b = 0) makes the parent inessential and gives β = 0, so exact zeros appear. Re-check essentiality and positive private counts after every matching.
- **Second overlap.** A holder that gains a second overlap of two or more names leaves the proved case and enters the three-in-a-row case, which is only a lead.
- **Matchings.** Count them up to names, as orbits, and close source relabelling before comparing counts.
- **Bootstrap.** Resample orbits under the declared weighting, not labelled copies.

## Census controls

- **Draws.** 128 draws give a standard error near 0.09 on C. The entries +2/50, +2/54 and +2/106 are invisible at that size; +2/106 needs on the order of 25,000 draws. Use draws for membership and sanity only, and exact tables for every multiplication or domination claim.
- **Cost.** The subset formula is 2^(holders) terms and trivial through 10 names. For second stages, factor it over shared distinctions, separate competing counts by certified bounds, and list the residue explicitly.
- **Parity control.** Its pair table is identically zero at width ≥ 3, so calling its membership a structural count is the right label.
